title: decode uses live_vocab (a COUNT of live rows) as the index where never-minted rows begin, so it masks the top len(retired_ids) LIVE token rows to -inf
failure: compose.py:338 binds `live_vocab` to `Vocabulary.live_size()`, which P4 defines as `len(id2bytes) - len(retired)`. Ran it: a Vocabulary with 280 minted ids and retired={260,261,262} gives live_size()=277, and `LM.decode(..., live_vocab=277, retired_ids={260,261,262})` returns -inf at ids [260,261,262,277,278,279] -- 277/278/279 are live, matchable tokens the tokenizer emits. The docstring's own example scale (probation arms: 224 of 256 minted tokens retired) means 224 live rows get -inf; any window whose target is one of them yields an infinite cross-entropy, and those tokens can never be predicted.
evidence: Body: `dead[int(live_vocab):] = True            # never minted: a suffix`. Docstring: "Never-minted rows are [live_vocab:]; RETIRED ROWS ARE BELOW live_vocab AND ARE NOT A SUFFIX" -- both sentences are only true if live_vocab is the minted-row COUNT. tok/api.py:`def live_size(self): return len(self.id2bytes) - len(self.retired)`; compose.py:338 "live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling". This is exactly the "a suffix rule would mask the wrong rows" failure the comment three lines below warns about, in the opposite direction.
fix: Start the never-minted suffix at the number of positional rows (`vocab.size()`), not the live count: either change the root's binding to pass `vocab.size()` under this spelling, or have decode take the minted count and mask `dead[minted:]` plus `dead[sorted(retired_ids)]`.
_triage_evidence: decode()'s masking code (lm/api.py:515-530) is functionally unchanged: `dead[int(live_vocab):] = True` still treats its argument as the boundary of minted rows. Ran it directly: with a 280-minted / 3-retired vocabulary, decode(..., live_vocab=Vocabulary.live_size()==277, retired_ids={260,261,262}) masks ids 277, 278 and 279 to -inf even though they are live, minted, matchable tokens; decode(..., live_vocab=Vocabulary.size()==280, ...) masks correctly.
_residue: a new explanatory comment was added inside decode() (lines 516-522) insisting the caller must pass Vocabulary.size(), not live_size() -- but spine/compose.py's own coupling table (round 1's cited evidence, line 338, outside this file's scope) is unchanged and still literally reads 'live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling,' so if that documented wiring is what the composition root actually uses, the exact failure round 1 measured still reproduces; decode() itself cannot be the site of a further fix since it already does what its own top-level docstring specifies

title: encode accepts n_layers and never uses it, so MEM's key-depth truncation is 100% inert -- the exact 'silently inert twice over' defect the docstring exists to end.
failure: MEM.key_depth is documented to arrive here as an argument so the memory-key path runs only the first n transformer blocks ("at LAYERS=12 the key path was paying twelve layers of attention over an 8-token window"). The body after the pos_max refusal never references `n_layers`: it always runs `model.body(h, ...)` in full. Verified on a 2-layer transformer (width 32, heads 4, ctx 8): `encode(..., n_layers=1)` and `encode(..., n_layers=0)` both differ from the full-stack output by max |dh| = 0.0. Consequence: the declared counter `lm.encode.key_path_truncated` can never be nonzero, MEM's key cost is whatever LM_LAYERS says, and the keys MEM stores are the full-depth hidden regardless of what key_depth is set to.
evidence: Signature `def encode(lm: Config, model, x, *, n_layers=None, extra=None)` (lm/api.py:397); body lines 449-461 contain no read of `n_layers`. Contract line contradicted: "n_layers runs only the first n blocks on the transformer arm, for the memory-key path (:1580-1593)... On the gru arm it is accepted and ignored, and that is a DECLARED GATE, not a silence -- CENSUS.md:250 records KEY_LAYERS as 'silently inert twice over'" (lm/api.py:415-421), plus "DID IT FIRE: ... lm.encode.key_path_truncated (n_layers actually reduced the stack)" (lm/api.py:432-433).
fix: On the transformer arm, when `n_layers` is not None, run only `model.body.layers[:n_layers]` (applying the same causal mask) and record `lm.encode.key_path_truncated`; on the gru arm record the declared unreachable Gate instead of silently ignoring the argument.
_triage_evidence: lm/api.py's encode() body (lines 431-457) never references `n_layers`. Ran it on a 2-layer transformer (width 32, heads 4, ctx 8): encode(cfg, model, x, n_layers=1) vs encode(cfg, model, x) gave max |diff| = 0.0. lm.encode.key_path_truncated can still never be nonzero.

title: encode accepts `extra` and never adds it, so WORLD's forecast conditioning term is silently discarded.
failure: `extra` is documented as "an optional additive term on the hidden state, (B, L, width) or None" whose whole purpose is to let WORLD.forecast condition the LM as a parameter instead of monkey-patching model.encode. The body never adds it. Verified: `encode(cfg, m, x, extra=torch.ones(2,8,32))` differs from `encode(cfg, m, x)` by max |dh| = 0.0. WORLD's forecast therefore conditions on nothing while believing it does, the returned hidden (and every logit decoded from it) is the unconditioned one, and the declared counter `lm.encode.extra_applied` can never fire.
evidence: Signature `def encode(lm: Config, model, x, *, n_layers=None, extra=None)` (lm/api.py:397); the body at lines 449-461 is `e = ...; h = model.drop(e + pos); h = model.body(h, ...); return h` with no use of `extra`. Contract contradicted: lm/api.py:423-428 ("It exists so WORLD's forecast can condition the LM as a PARAMETER rather than by rebinding model.encode: the monkey-patch at :4158-4169 let a timing probe... A timing probe decided the run.") and lm/api.py:434 ("lm.encode.extra_applied").
fix: Add the term where the contract puts it -- on the hidden state, e.g. `h = h + extra` after the body (validating extra.shape == h.shape and extra.device == h.device) -- and set `lm.encode.extra_applied` when it is not None.
_triage_evidence: Same body, same test run: encode(cfg, model, x, extra=torch.ones(2,8,32)*5.0) vs encode(cfg, model, x) gave max |diff| = 0.0. `extra` is not referenced anywhere in the function.

title: Nothing in the new bodies seeds torch's global generator, so at LM_DROPOUT>0 two runs at the same RUN_SEED diverge and G2's determinism floor absorbs the difference
failure: LM_DROPOUT=0.2, LM_ARCH=transformer. `self.drop = nn.Dropout(geom.dropout)` (:106) and `nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(dropout=geom.dropout)` (:114-119) draw their forward-time masks from torch's DEFAULT global generator, which torch seeds from OS entropy at first use and which no code in this tree ever calls torch.manual_seed on (only train/levers.py:277 mentions the old call, as a defect being removed). Measured: three processes printed torch.initial_seed() = 13989758112835367564 / 4786972063193561826 / 11264655507350687211. Running the identical script twice at RUN_SEED=0, LM.encode() on a zero batch summed to -92.9096450805664 and -102.38495635986328. So the trajectory is not a function of the seed. train/levers.py:290-292 says G2's test_determinism 'runs two identical seeded CPU runs to establish the measured float noise floor that every isolation result is read against' -- with dropout on, that floor is inflated by whole dropout masks and every isolation verdict is read against a threshold that is not a noise floor.
evidence: lm/api.py:106 `self.drop = nn.Dropout(geom.dropout)`; :114-119 `nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(..., dropout=geom.dropout, ...)`. train/levers.py:272-273 declares seed as 'Root seed for the whole run; every module's initialisation and the data stream derive from it.' spine/rng.py:265-284 supplies Rng.torch_generator() for exactly this interop and no call site in src/ uses it; `grep -rn manual_seed src/` finds only the three raw `torch.Generator(device="cpu")` seeds in lm/sig/fabric build, none of which reaches nn.Dropout.
fix: Seed the process-global torch stream once, from the run seed, in RUN.process_setup (which already owns 'the process-wide arithmetic settings ONCE, before any package is built'): `torch.manual_seed(spine.rng.derive_seed("torch.global", int(run.seed)))`, and record it on Process so the banner can print it. nn.Dropout takes no generator, so a per-subsystem stream cannot cover it; the alternative is to state in the contract that the run is only reproducible at dropout=0.
_triage_evidence: `grep -rn manual_seed src/` finds only the three package-local `torch.Generator(device=...)` seedings (fabric/sig/lm build) plus one dead comment in train/levers.py noting the old global `torch.manual_seed` call was removed; no call anywhere seeds torch's process-global generator. train/api.py's process_setup (lines 160-200) sets TF32/AMP flags only, no manual_seed. Ran it in two fresh processes at the same RUN_SEED=0, LM_DROPOUT=0.2, transformer arch: torch.initial_seed() printed 14029224735880684544 and 4654533202693680726 (different), and LM.encode() on an identical zero batch summed to -50.40 and -96.44 respectively.

title: encode silently ignores both n_layers and extra, so the memory-key depth cut and WORLD's forecast conditioning do nothing
failure: Ran it: `encode(cfg, m, x, n_layers=1)` and `encode(cfg, m, x, extra=torch.ones(2,8,32)*5.0)` both return tensors byte-identical to `encode(cfg, m, x)`. So (a) MEM.key_depth's n_layers cut never happens -- at LM_LAYERS=12 the key path still pays twelve layers of attention over an 8-token window, the exact cost the docstring cites; (b) WORLD's forecast term is dropped on the floor while the caller believes the LM was conditioned, which is a wrong hidden state feeding MEM's keys and FAB's router with nothing anywhere saying so. The documented surfaces lm.encode.key_path_truncated and lm.encode.extra_applied can never be nonzero.
evidence: Signature `def encode(lm: Config, model, x, *, n_layers=None, extra=None)`; the body between lines 436 and 461 never mentions `n_layers` or `extra`. Docstring: "n_layers runs only the first n blocks on the transformer arm ... On the gru arm it is accepted and ignored, and that is a DECLARED GATE, not a silence" and "`extra` is an optional additive term on the hidden state ... so WORLD's forecast can condition the LM as a PARAMETER rather than by rebinding model.encode".
fix: Add `h = h + extra` after the embedding sum (shape-checked against (B, L, width)), run `model.body.layers[:n_layers]` on the transformer arm when n_layers is not None, and emit the two documented gates -- including the gru arm's declared accepted-and-ignored gate rather than silence.
_triage_evidence: Duplicate of the n_layers/extra findings above at the same function; both arguments remain completely unused in encode()'s body. Same test: both n_layers=1 and extra=<nonzero tensor> produce max |diff| = 0.0 against the default call.

title: On the transformer arm LM.encode's return DOES carry dropout, so MEM's keys are written dropped in train mode and queried undropped at eval -- the defect Q-LM-9 claims to have removed
failure: LM_ARCH=transformer, LM_DROPOUT>0. nn.TransformerEncoderLayer with norm_first=True computes `x = x + self._ff_block(self.norm2(x))` where _ff_block ends in dropout2, so the LAST layer's output dropout is on encode()'s return path. Measured: built the model at LM_DROPOUT=0.2, arch=transformer, then set `m.drop.p = 0.0` to disable the embedding-dropout site and called encode twice in train mode -- the two returns still differ; in eval mode they are equal, and the train-mode value differs from the eval-mode one. compose.py binds key_fn to LM.encode, so at dropout>0 the store is written with regularised keys during the loop and read with unregularised ones at eval, and FAB's router sees a different input in train and eval.
evidence: Docstring :215-216 and body comment :457-459: 'UNDROPPED ON THE WAY OUT. Three packages consume this -- MEM as keys, FAB as routing input, LM as the readout source -- and a value three packages consume must not carry one consumer's regulariser.' build_model's docstring :280-289 claims the three sites are 'the embedding dropout, the inter-layer dropout at depth > 1, and the READOUT dropout, applied inside decode()' and that this 'makes the key path train/eval consistent STRUCTURALLY rather than by convention'. On the transformer arm there is a fourth site nobody chose: `nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(..., dropout=geom.dropout, ..., norm_first=True)` at lm/api.py:114-119, whose last layer drops the value returned at :461.
fix: Either state the arm difference in the contract, or make it structural: run the encoder body's last layer without its output dropout (e.g. build the stack with dropout=0.0 on the final layer, or apply the encoder under a `torch.nn.utils` dropout-off scope for the key path). A `for_key=` keyword is explicitly forbidden by the docstring, so the fix belongs in the constructor at :114-119, not at the call site.
_triage_evidence: lm/api.py:117 still passes `dropout=geom.dropout` into nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(..., norm_first=True), and encode() (lines 445-457) returns model.body(h,...) directly with nothing stripping that layer's internal dropout before return. Ran it: built at LM_DROPOUT=0.2, arch=transformer, set model.drop.p=0.0 (disabling ONLY the embedding-dropout site) and called encode() twice in train mode on the same input under no_grad -- the two outputs still differed (not equal); in eval mode two calls were identical to each other and different from the train-mode value. This proves the transformer body's own internal dropout (not model.drop) is still leaking onto encode()'s returned hidden state.

title: build_model's own frozen contract still names the stream "lm" as its seeding source and DID-IT-FIRE surface, but the repair moved the actual draw to a child stream "lm.init" without updating the docstring -- the documented verification surface can no longer distinguish build_model having run from it never being called.
failure: Any reader or tool that follows this entry point's own contract to check whether LM.build_model fired. The docstring at line 287-288 still reads 'Seeding: calls spine.rng.rng_for("lm", seed) and initialises every tensor from that one stream' and the DID IT FIRE line at 300 still names `rng.issued()["lm"]`, but the repaired body (line 310) draws from `rng_for("lm.init", int(seed))` instead -- "lm" is never touched by build_model any more. Since RUN.streams mints every name in compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS (which includes "lm") unconditionally at step 0 regardless of whether build_model is ever called, `rng.issued()["lm"]` is present in every process either way and carries no information about build_model having run. Verified: after RUN.streams(...) alone (no build_model call), `rng.issued()` already contains 'lm'; after also calling LM.build_model, `rng.issued()` gains 'lm.init' as a second, separately-seeded entry ((7250686939781505743, 0) for "lm" vs (4933293191311707615, 0) for "lm.init") while "lm"'s registration is byte-identical to the pre-build_model state. A reader who checks the documented surface exactly as written cannot tell 'build_model fired' from 'build_model was never called' -- the armed-vs-fired distinction this project's own DID IT FIRE convention exists to preserve collapses for this one entry point, and it collapses specifically because the repair fixed the code and not the contract describing it.
evidence: src/lm/api.py:287-288 ("Seeding: calls spine.rng.rng_for(\"lm\", seed)...") and :300 ("rng.issued()[\"lm\"]") are unchanged text from before the repair (git show b95c4a4 -- src/lm/api.py's diff hunk spans these exact lines and shows neither was edited). The body at :310 (`stream = _rng.rng_for("lm.init", int(seed))`) was changed by that same commit specifically to stop touching "lm" (see the comment immediately above it: 'A CHILD OF THE DECLARED PARENT, NOT A SECOND "lm"'). `grep -rn '"lm"' src/` confirms no code anywhere still calls `rng_for("lm", ...)`; the only surviving references to the bare name "lm" are these two stale docstring lines and the RNG_SUBSYSTEMS tuple in spine/compose.py that mints it at step 0 independent of build_model.
fix: Update line 287-288 to describe seeding via `rng_for("lm.init", seed)` (a child of the "lm" RUN.streams mints and never draws from), and change line 300's DID IT FIRE row to `rng.issued()["lm.init"]`, noting that "lm" itself is expected to report zero draws forever by design.

title: The compose branch of decode drops the bias term its own docstring specifies.
failure: Under lm.compose the docstring states the readout is "`h @ table.t() + bias` from the tied composed table"; the body computes `logits = h @ table.t()` with no bias, and no bias parameter is constructed on the compose arm (_LM.__init__ builds `emb`/`head` only when `not geom.compose`). When the ByteComposer lands, LM_COMPOSE=1 will produce a strictly bias-free softmax while the banner and the checkpoint describe a decoder with a per-row bias, which shifts every logit and every reported bits/byte relative to the non-compose arm the numbers are compared against. Currently masked by `_LM.composed_table` raising NotImplementedError, so it is latent rather than firing.
evidence: lm/api.py:507-509 `if model.compose: table = model.token_table(); logits = h @ table.t()` against lm/api.py:481 "Under compose it is `h @ table.t() + bias` from the tied composed table; otherwise the head Linear." _LM.__init__ (lm/api.py:106-108) constructs `self.head = nn.Linear(w, v)` only under `if not geom.compose`, so no bias exists for the compose arm to add.
fix: Allocate a `(vocab_slots,)` output bias on the compose arm in _LM.__init__ (it is not part of the tied table and does not reintroduce the L13 dead weight) and add it here, or amend the docstring to state that the composed readout is bias-free.
_triage_evidence: lm/api.py:503-507 is unchanged: `if model.compose: table = model.token_table(); logits = h @ table.t()`, no bias. No output-bias parameter is constructed in _LM.__init__ for the compose arm. decode()'s docstring (line 473) still promises 'h @ table.t() + bias'.
_residue: still latent: _LM.composed_table() (line 128-132) still raises NotBuilt, so this branch cannot actually execute until the ByteComposer (a separate, still-stubbed TOK-side piece) lands -- same as round 1's own characterisation

title: LMGeometry carries no record of whether the layer count came from the 0 sentinel, so lm.resolve.layers_from_sentinel cannot be reported
failure: `layers = _SENTINEL_DEPTH.get(arch, 1) if declared_layers == 0 else declared_layers` and LMGeometry stores only the resolved `layers`. A run at LM_ARCH=transformer LM_LAYERS=0 and one at LM_LAYERS=4 produce an identical LMGeometry and an identical geometry manifest, so the report cannot make the statement the contract asks for -- which number the run actually used -- even though that is the exact confusion ("a reader could not tell what depth a saved model was") the paragraph above it cites.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: lm.resolve.calls (must be exactly 1 per process), lm.resolve.layers_from_sentinel (1 when cfg.layers == 0 -- proves which number the run actually used)". LMGeometry fields: arch, width, layers, heads, ctx, pos_max, vocab_slots, compose, dropout, max_token_bytes, param_estimate.
fix: Add a `layers_from_sentinel: bool` (or the declared value beside the resolved one) to LMGeometry so LM.counters can report it, and count resolve() calls.
_triage_evidence: LMGeometry's dataclass fields (lm/api.py:60-70) are unchanged: arch, width, layers, heads, ctx, pos_max, vocab_slots, compose, dropout, max_token_bytes, param_estimate -- no layers_from_sentinel field or equivalent. resolve() (lines 168-224) computes `layers` and discards whether declared_layers was 0.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area

title: encode reads lm.ctx while declaring "LEVERS READ: none directly"
failure: The pos-overflow refusal interpolates `int(lm.ctx)` into its message, so encode does read an LM lever on the refusal path -- the one path where a reader most needs the contract to be accurate about where the number came from. The declared list says the function reads no lever directly, and the value it prints is a lever read rather than the wire it names in the same sentence.
evidence: Docstring: "LEVERS READ: none directly / WIRES READ: d_pos_max". Body line 445: `f"{pos_max} row(s) (LM_CTX={int(lm.ctx)} through the d_pos_max wire). Refused rather "`.
fix: Either name `ctx` in encode's LEVERS READ, or print only `d_pos_max` and let the wire ledger say where it came from.
_triage_evidence: encode()'s LEVERS READ line (lm/api.py:425) is unchanged: 'LEVERS READ: none directly'. The pos-overflow refusal at line 441 still interpolates `int(lm.ctx)` into its message.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area

title: the dead-row mask is rebuilt on every decode call although the contract specifies it is cached
failure: Every call allocates a bool tensor of vocab_slots, and when anything is retired also `torch.tensor(sorted(retired_ids))`, then a masked_fill -- once per window on the hot path, at LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=16384 with hundreds of retired ids on the probation arms. The documented cache key exists precisely because both inputs are monotone, so the rebuild is pure waste that the contract already ruled out.
evidence: Docstring: "The mask is cached on (live_vocab, len(retired_ids)); both only ever grow." Body lines 519-526 build `dead` and `idx` unconditionally on each call. The same docstring's "LEVERS READ: mask_dead_rows, vocab_slots, compose" also names two levers the body never reads (it uses model.compose and logits.shape[-1]).
fix: Memoise the mask on the model keyed by (live_vocab, len(retired_ids)) and reuse it, and correct the LEVERS READ line to the one lever actually read.
_triage_evidence: decode()'s docstring (line 487) still says 'The mask is cached on (live_vocab, len(retired_ids)); both only ever grow,' but the body (lines 515-529) allocates a fresh `dead = torch.zeros(...)` tensor and, when retired_ids is non-empty, a fresh `torch.tensor(sorted(retired_ids), ...)` on every single call, with no cache keyed on the model or elsewhere.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area
